Public Portion 
 1. Continued Discussions on the Woodland Ordinance 
On November 9, 2026, the Sustainability and Environment Committee, chaired by Councilor 
Victor Davila, met to continue reviewing the proposed Urban Woodlands Ordinance. Discussion 
focused on tree replacement requirements, associated costs, property exemptions, and 
enforcement procedures. Concerns were raised regarding the proposed replacement cost of 
approximately $700 per tree and its potential impact on property owners and smaller 
developments. A reduced amount of approximately $300 per tree and an annual review of 
replacement costs were considered. The committee also reviewed a proposed exemption for 
owner-occupied one-, two-, and three-family properties involving the removal of no more than 
nine established private shade trees. 
 
The committee discussed establishing an Urban Woodlands Commission to assist with oversight 
and administration of the ordinance. Additional matters included enforcement responsibilities, 
statutory fine limitations, potential penalties for unauthorized tree removal, and procedures for 
verifying replacement plantings. The Law Department agreed to further review the legal 
feasibility of additional penalties and clarify enforcement and compliance requirements. 
Questions regarding the proposed commission's authority to rescind permits remained 
unresolved. 
 
The Law Department was tasked with incorporating applicable revisions into an updated 
ordinance draft, including provisions addressing tree replacement verification and enforcement 
procedures. Councilor Davila expressed the intention to introduce the proposed ordinance to the 
full City Council at its next regular meeting, subject to completion of revisions and submission 
deadlines. Proposed fees, penalties, and administrative provisions remained under review. The 
meeting adjourned at 5:32 p.m.
